newsitem.title: USA: Virginia woman asks for clemency for son's killer.
newsitem.headline: Virginia woman asks for clemency for son's killer.

text.p: Virginia's attorney general on Thursday opposed a request to halt the execution of a convicted killer who was found to have also murdered an inmate 11 years ago.

The filing with the U.S. Supreme Court to carry out the execution of Joseph Payne followed impassioned requests this week by his lawyers and the mother of the murdered inmate. Payne was scheduled to die by lethal injection on Nov. 7.

Reba Dunford, whose son, David, burned to death in his locked prison cell, appealed to Virginia Gov. George Allen to spare Payne's life. A meeting of Payne's attorneys and the governor's staff was scheduled for Nov. 4.

Payne is one of nine Virginia inmates with execution dates before the end of the year in a state that ranks third in the country in executions -- 32 since reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976 -- behind Texas and Florida.
"I don't want Joe Payne to die. It won't do anyone any good if he is killed," Dunford said in a sworn affidavit sent on Tuesday to Allen.
"Joe Payne's execution will do nothing but hurt more people, including me. I can think of no greater tragedy than killing an innocent man," she wrote.

Payne was convicted of capital murder in the killing of David Dunford, 28, who was serving 15 years for burglary at Virginia's Powhatan Correctional Centre, near Richmond. Payne was there serving a life sentence for the 1981 robbery and capital murder of a Prince William County store owner.

Payne was convicted of the inmate's death primarily on the testimony of another convict, Robert "Dirty Smitty" Smith, who testified that on March 3, 1985, he saw Payne put a padlock on David Dunford's cell door, throw flammable liquid and then a match through the cell bars. Dunford died nine days later.

In her affidavit, Reba Dunford, who lives in Loudoun County in Northern Virginia, wrote: "Too many people have come forward and said that Robert Smith lied about Joe Payne. I have doubts that Joe Payne killed my son."
She concluded: "Please do not let this happen ... it would be a terrible mistake and one that I could not live with."
